For RGAA test 1.1.3. Faults an image button only when it has none of the four sources the methodology lists; it never answers no_fault. Elements: every HTML <input> element whose type attribute is an ASCII case-insensitive match for "image", in the top document and in every document nested in it through frames, open and closed shadow trees included (read through the DevTools protocol). A string is blank when it is empty or made only of ASCII whitespace (U+0009, U+000A, U+000C, U+000D, U+0020). For each element, in this order: (1) It is in a document nested through a frame, not in the top document or a shadow tree of it: cannot_tell, since this test does not say whether a framed document is part of the page. (2) Its type attribute value is not exactly the lowercase string "image": cannot_tell. (3) It has a role attribute, whatever its value: cannot_tell. (4) It is hidden or not drawn: computed display none on it or an ancestor in the flat tree; computed visibility other than visible; the hidden or inert attribute on it or an ancestor; an aria-hidden attribute with any value other than false (ignoring ASCII case and surrounding whitespace) on it or an ancestor; absent from the accessibility tree or ignored in it; computed opacity 0 on it or an ancestor; checkVisibility() with the options contentVisibilityAuto, opacityProperty and visibilityProperty returns false; no part of its border box at least 4 by 4 CSS pixels lies inside the viewport of the page as loaded and inside every ancestor that clips it (overflow other than visible, the clip property, clip-path); or, at the centre of that visible part, the topmost element found by hit-testing is neither the element nor a descendant of it: cannot_tell, since the text of this test gives no exception for such buttons and does not say whether they count. A button below the fold is therefore never a witness. (5) It has an aria-labelledby attribute that is not blank, whatever it resolves to: cannot_tell. (6) Its aria-label, alt or title attribute is present and not blank: cannot_tell, since one of the listed sources may hold, and whether it does (for title, whether assistive technologies render it, as the glossary asks) is not decided here. This includes values made only of invisible characters other than ASCII whitespace, such as no-break or zero-width spaces. (7) It has a value attribute that is not blank, or one or more associated <label> elements (its labels list is not empty): cannot_tell. These are not listed sources, but the glossary says that where the name computation is only partly supported, the value assistive technologies really render is the alternative, and a browser may expose such text. (8) Otherwise, every one of aria-labelledby, aria-label, alt and title is absent or blank, and there is no value text and no label: fault on that element. Page result: fault if any element falls under (8); otherwise cannot_tell if any element falls under (1) to (7), or if a nested document or a shadow tree cannot be read; otherwise inapplicable, since the page has no <input> of type image. Never no_fault.

For RGAA test 1.2.1, evidence only: it never decides whether an image is decorative or has a caption, so its fault never proves the test fails. Elements: every HTML element in the top document and in every document nested in it through frames, open and closed shadow trees included (read through the DevTools protocol). A string is blank when it is empty or made only of ASCII whitespace (U+0009, U+000A, U+000C, U+000D, U+0020). For each , in this order: (1) It has no alt attribute, or its alt value is not the empty string (a value made of spaces is not empty here): not examined. (2) It has an aria-hidden attribute whose value, with surrounding ASCII whitespace removed, is an ASCII case-insensitive match for "true", or a role attribute whose first token (split on ASCII whitespace, compared ignoring ASCII case) is "presentation" or "none": not examined, since another route of the test holds for it. (3) It has an aria-label attribute that is not blank, an aria-labelledby attribute that is not blank (whatever it resolves to), or a title attribute that is not blank: fault on that element. The fault records which of these attributes are present and their values, and whether the element is rendered (computed display other than none on it and its ancestors in the flat tree, computed visibility visible) and present and not ignored in the accessibility tree; hidden images are reported too, as evidence. (4) Otherwise: no fault on that element. Page result: fault if any element falls under (3); otherwise cannot_tell if the page holds any , or if a nested document or a shadow tree cannot be read; otherwise inapplicable. Never no_fault: the test applies only to decorative images without a caption, which this check cannot identify.

For RGAA test 1.2.4, the condition on <title> and <desc> only, and evidence only: it never decides whether an image is decorative or has a caption, so its fault never proves the test fails. Elements: every <svg> element in the SVG namespace, in the top document and in every document nested in it through frames, open and closed shadow trees included (read through the DevTools protocol), that has its own aria-hidden attribute whose value, with surrounding ASCII whitespace removed, is an ASCII case-insensitive match for "true". For each such <svg>: if it has a descendant <title> or <desc> element in the SVG namespace whose text content (textContent) contains at least one character other than ASCII whitespace (U+0009, U+000A, U+000C, U+000D, U+0020), fault on the <svg>, recording each such element and its text, and whether the <svg> is rendered. Content displayed through a <use> element is not followed. Otherwise: no fault on that <svg>. Page result: fault if any <svg> is faulted; otherwise cannot_tell if the page holds any such <svg>, or if a nested document or a shadow tree cannot be read; otherwise inapplicable. Never no_fault: the test applies only to decorative vector images without a caption, and an svg with aria-hidden="true" may be informative and wrongly hidden, or captioned.

For RGAA test 1.3.9, evidence only: it measures length and never decides whether an image carries information, is a CAPTCHA or an image-test, or whether an alternative is concise, so its fault never proves the test fails. Elements, in the top document and in every document nested in it through frames, open and closed shadow trees included (read through the DevTools protocol): ; any element whose role attribute's first token (split on ASCII whitespace, compared ignoring ASCII case) is "img"; ; whose type attribute is an ASCII case-insensitive match for "image";

For RGAA test 1.3.1, the alt attribute of only, and evidence only: it never decides whether an image carries information or whether an alternative is relevant, so its fault never proves the test fails. Elements: every HTML element that has an alt attribute, in the top document and in every document nested in it through frames, open and closed shadow trees included (read through the DevTools protocol). Let v be the alt value with leading and trailing ASCII whitespace (U+0009, U+000A, U+000C, U+000D, U+0020) removed. Fault on the element when v is not empty and either (a) v contains no ASCII whitespace and ends, compared ignoring ASCII case, with a full stop followed by one of jpg, jpeg, png, gif, webp, avif, svg, bmp, ico, tif or tiff; or (b) the element's src attribute parses as a URL whose path has a last segment that, percent-decoded, is not empty and is exactly equal to v. The fault records v, the src and whether the element is rendered and exposed in the accessibility tree. Otherwise: no fault on that element. Page result: fault if any element is faulted; otherwise cannot_tell if the page holds any with an alt attribute, or if a nested document or a shadow tree cannot be read; otherwise inapplicable. Never no_fault: a file name is a strong sign of an alternative written without regard to the image, but the image may be decorative, a CAPTCHA or image-test, the only content of a link or button, or one whose file name happens to say what it shows.

For RGAA test 1.9.5, condition 3 (wording line 4, the aria-label of the figure) only, on images captioned by a figure and figcaption. Scope: the top-level document as rendered on the target, light tree only; documents in frames and content in shadow trees are not examined. A witness is a pair of a figure element F in the HTML namespace and an image element I that meets every condition below. (a) I is a canvas element in the HTML namespace; I is a descendant of F and not of C. (b) F has exactly one figcaption descendant, C, and C is a child of F. (c) Apart from C and its descendants, every element inside F is I, a descendant of I, a source child of a picture element that contains I, or an ancestor of I that is a picture, div or span element with no role, aria-*, tabindex or contenteditable attribute; no element inside F, F included, is a shadow host; every text node inside F that is outside C and outside I holds only ASCII whitespace; and the computed content of the ::before and ::after pseudo-elements of F and of each such ancestor of I is none or normal. So F holds I, C and nothing else a caption could belong to. (d) Neither F nor any ancestor of F carries aria-hidden="true", inert or hidden, is a button element, or has a role attribute whose first token the browser recognises is img or button. (e) C is present and not ignored in the browser's accessibility tree; its text content holds at least one Unicode letter or number (general category L or N); and it has no descendant that is an a, button, input, select, textarea or details element, or that has a tabindex or role attribute, so that it is not a control such as a link to a larger view. (f) I is present and not ignored in the accessibility tree; it has no role attribute whose first recognised token is none or presentation; it has no aria-labelledby and no aria-describedby attribute; if it is an img or input element, it has no alt attribute whose value is empty or only ASCII whitespace; and its computed accessible name holds at least one Unicode letter or number. (g) C and I are each visible: computed visibility visible on each, computed opacity 1 on each and on every ancestor, no filter, mask or clip-path on either or on an ancestor, and each has a part at least 4 pixels square that lies inside the page's scrollable area and inside every clipping ancestor. On each witness the check reads F's aria-label attribute and C. Fault on the witness when (1) F has no aria-label attribute, whatever else names it: technical note 3 rules out aria-labelledby, and technical note 1 makes aria-label the minimum; or (2) F's aria-label value holds no Unicode letter or number, while C does; or (3) C has no element child, the computed content of C's ::before and ::after is none or normal, and the sequence of letters and numbers of F's aria-label differs from that of C's text content, each taken in order after Unicode NFKC normalisation and full case folding, with every other character dropped. Contents whose letters and numbers differ are not identical under any reading. Any other witness is not faulted: an aria-label whose letters and numbers match C's may still differ in spacing, punctuation or case, and a caption with element children or generated content may have a content that differs from its text nodes. Pairs that fail any of (a) to (g) are left undecided on purpose: an image treated as decorative (empty alt, presentational role, empty name, hidden), because the glossary lets an image whose caption can serve as its replacement text be treated as decorative with no figure, which is the condition's only exception; an image or caption that is hidden, invisible or off-screen, because the test gives no exception for them and does not say whether they count; a figure that holds anything else, because its figcaption may caption that instead; an image named or described through aria-labelledby or aria-describedby; anything in a frame or a shadow tree. A captioned image that is not in a figure with a figcaption is never examined: recognising a caption elsewhere is judgment. Page result: fault if any witness is a fault, naming each F; otherwise cannot_tell. The check never answers no_fault or inapplicable.

For each remaining field, in this order: (1) not rendered (computed display none on it or an ancestor, computed visibility hidden or collapse), or it or an ancestor has aria-hidden="true" or is inert: cannot_tell. (2) It has no aria-labelledby attribute, no aria-label attribute, no title attribute, an empty labels list (no <label> whose for equals its id in its tree, and no <label> ancestor that labels it), and no <label> ancestor at all: fault. Every condition of the test needs one of these, so the field meets none. (3) Otherwise cannot_tell: the check does not decide whether a present mechanism is sufficient (empty values, references to missing ids, a label without for, the adjacent-button condition). Page result: fault if any field has a fault; otherwise cannot_tell if there is any field; inapplicable when there is none.

For RGAA test 11.1.2. Evidence only. Elements: every <label> element with a for attribute, in the top document and every readable document nested in it through frames, shadow trees included. Fault on a label when its for value is empty, or when no element in the same tree (the document, or the shadow root holding the label) has an id equal to its for value: the label is tied to no element by for and id. The fault does not say which field the label was meant for, or that it was meant for a field at all. Page result: fault if any label has a fault; otherwise no_fault if at least one label has a for attribute; inapplicable when none has.

For RGAA test 11.2.3, the empty-aria-label case only; whether a non-empty aria-label is relevant is not examined. Elements: in the top document and every document nested in it through frames, shadow trees included, every element with an aria-label attribute that is a form field as the glossary lists it: <input> with no type attribute or of type text, password, search, email, number, tel, url, checkbox, radio, date, range, color, time, month, week, datetime-local or file (type compared ignoring ASCII case), <textarea>, <select>, <output>, <progress>, <meter>, <datalist>, <optgroup>, <option>, and elements with an explicit role of progressbar, slider, spinbutton, textbox, listbox, searchbox, combobox, option, checkbox, radio or switch. Elements that are not fields under the glossary (<input> of type submit, reset, hidden, image or button, <button>, role="button") are skipped. For each field, in this order: (1) It is not an <input> of a type in the list above, a <textarea> or a <select> (it is another listed element, or an <input> of an unlisted type): cannot_tell. Elements with a role may take a name from their content when aria-label is empty, and no other kind is needed for the fault. (2) It is not rendered (computed display none on it or an ancestor, computed visibility hidden or collapse, or inside a frame element that is not rendered); or it is not exposed in the accessibility tree (aria-hidden="true" or inert on it, an ancestor or a hosting frame element); or it is not visible: computed opacity 0 on it or an ancestor, or no part of it at least 4 pixels square lies inside the page's scrollable area and inside every clipping ancestor: cannot_tell. The test gives no exception for such fields, but whether a hidden or invisible field (an anti-spam trap, a styled replacement) is one the test covers is open. (3) It has an aria-labelledby attribute, whatever its value, or at least one associated <label> element (its labels list is not empty), or a title or a placeholder attribute: cannot_tell. The glossary's order of the accessible name puts aria-labelledby before aria-label, and does not say whether an empty aria-label gives way to a <label> or a title. (4) Its aria-label value is empty or made only of ASCII whitespace (U+0009, U+000A, U+000C, U+000D, U+0020): fault on the field. The aria-label is its only label mechanism, and its content is empty, so it cannot let the user know the field's function. (5) Otherwise cannot_tell: whether a non-empty aria-label is relevant is judgment. This includes a value made only of other invisible characters, such as no-break or zero-width spaces. Page result: fault if any field falls under (4); otherwise cannot_tell if any field was examined, or if a nested document cannot be read; otherwise inapplicable. Never no_fault.

For RGAA test 11.2.5. Evidence only: a hint that a field's aria-label may not contain its visible label. Elements: in the top document and every readable document nested in it through frames, shadow trees included, every with no type attribute or of type text, password, search, email, number, tel, url, date, time, month, week, datetime-local or file, every

For RGAA test 11.2.4. Evidence only: whether the elements a field's aria-labelledby references are empty. For RGAA test 11.2.2, the empty-title case only; whether a non-empty title is relevant is not examined. Elements: in the top document and every document nested in it through frames, shadow trees included, every element with a title attribute that is a form field as the glossary lists it: <input> with no type attribute or of type text, password, search, email, number, tel, url, checkbox, radio, date, range, color, time, month, week, datetime-local or file (type compared ignoring ASCII case), <textarea>, <select>, <output>, <progress>, <meter>, <datalist>, <optgroup>, <option>, and elements with an explicit role of progressbar, slider, spinbutton, textbox, listbox, searchbox, combobox, option, checkbox, radio or switch. Elements that are not fields under the glossary (<input> of type submit, reset, hidden, image or button, <button>, role="button") are skipped. For each field, in this order: (1) It is not an <input> of a type in the list above, a <textarea> or a <select> (it is another listed element, or an <input> of an unlisted type): cannot_tell. (2) It is not rendered (computed display none on it or an ancestor, computed visibility hidden or collapse, or inside a frame element that is not rendered); or it is not exposed in the accessibility tree (aria-hidden="true" or inert on it, an ancestor or a hosting frame element); or it is not visible: computed opacity 0 on it or an ancestor, or no part of it at least 4 pixels square lies inside the page's scrollable area and inside every clipping ancestor: cannot_tell. The test gives no exception for such fields, but whether a hidden or invisible field (an anti-spam trap, a styled replacement) is one the test covers is open. (3) It has an aria-labelledby or an aria-label attribute, whatever its value, or at least one associated <label> element (its labels list is not empty), or a placeholder attribute: cannot_tell. The glossary's order of the accessible name puts aria-labelledby, aria-label and <label> before title, so the title may not be the field's label; and the glossary says a placeholder may be rendered in place of the title. (4) Its title value is empty or made only of ASCII whitespace (U+0009, U+000A, U+000C, U+000D, U+0020): fault on the field. The title is its only label mechanism, and its content is empty, so it cannot let the user know the field's function. (5) Otherwise cannot_tell: whether a non-empty title is relevant is judgment. This includes a value made only of other invisible characters, such as no-break or zero-width spaces. Page result: fault if any field falls under (4); otherwise cannot_tell if any field was examined, or if a nested document cannot be read; otherwise inapplicable. Never no_fault.

For RGAA test 11.4.3. Evidence only: a hint that a checkbox's or radio button's label is not placed where the test puts it. Whether the label is close enough to the field, and whether a particular case of criterion 11.4 applies (among them a checkbox or radio button not presented visually as one), are not examined. Elements: in the top document and every readable document nested in it through frames, shadow trees included, every <input> of type checkbox or radio (type compared ignoring ASCII case) that is inside a <form> element or an element with an explicit role="form" (criterion 11.4 applies in each form), is rendered and exposed in the accessibility tree, and has exactly one associated <label> element, tied to it by a for attribute equal to its id and not containing it. Elements with role checkbox, radio or switch cannot have such a label and are not examined. For each field: cannot_tell when the field or its label has computed opacity 0 on itself or an ancestor, or has no part at least 4 pixels square inside the page's scrollable area and inside every clipping ancestor. Reading direction of the label: left to right when its rendered text holds a character of Unicode bidirectional class L and none of class R or AL; right to left when it holds a character of class R or AL and none of class L; cannot_tell otherwise (a label mixing both, or with no letter). Also cannot_tell when the labels of the fields examined in the same form are not all of one direction. Take the border boxes of the label (Lb) and of the field (Fb), with a tolerance of 2 pixels: the label is above when Lb.bottom <= Fb.top + 2, below when Lb.top >= Fb.bottom - 2, left when Lb.right <= Fb.left + 2, right when Lb.left >= Fb.right - 2. Fault on the field when its label is left to right, neither below nor right, and above or left; or right to left, neither below nor left, and above or right. When the label is in none of the four positions (the boxes overlap), cannot_tell. Otherwise no fault for that field. Page result: fault if any field has a fault; otherwise cannot_tell if any field got cannot_tell or a nested document cannot be read; otherwise no_fault if at least one field was examined; inapplicable if none was.

For RGAA test 11.4.2. Evidence only: a hint that a field's label is not placed where the test puts it. Whether the label is close enough to the field, and whether a particular case of criterion 11.4 applies, are not examined. Elements: in the top document and every readable document nested in it through frames, shadow trees included, every <input> with no type attribute or of type text, password, search, email, number, tel, url, date, range, color, time, month, week, datetime-local or file, every <textarea> and every <select>, that is inside a <form> element or an element with an explicit role="form" (criterion 11.4 applies in each form), is rendered and exposed in the accessibility tree, and has exactly one associated <label> element, tied to it by a for attribute equal to its id and not containing it. Fields given role checkbox, radio or switch are not examined. For each field: cannot_tell when the field or its label has computed opacity 0 on itself or an ancestor, or has no part at least 4 pixels square inside the page's scrollable area and inside every clipping ancestor. Reading direction of the label: left to right when its rendered text holds a character of Unicode bidirectional class L and none of class R or AL; right to left when it holds a character of class R or AL and none of class L; cannot_tell otherwise (a label mixing both, or with no letter). Also cannot_tell when the labels of the fields examined in the same form are not all of one direction. Take the border boxes of the label (Lb) and of the field (Fb), with a tolerance of 2 pixels: the label is above when Lb.bottom <= Fb.top + 2, below when Lb.top >= Fb.bottom - 2, left when Lb.right <= Fb.left + 2, right when Lb.left >= Fb.right - 2. Fault on the field when its label is left to right, neither above nor left, and below or right; or right to left, neither above nor right, and below or left. When the label is in none of the four positions (the boxes overlap, as with a label drawn inside the field), cannot_tell. Otherwise no fault for that field. Page result: fault if any field has a fault; otherwise cannot_tell if any field got cannot_tell or a nested document cannot be read; otherwise no_fault if at least one field was examined; inapplicable if none was.

For RGAA test 11.5.1. Evidence only: a hint that a set of radio buttons is not grouped by any means the test accepts. Whether grouping is necessary (the glossary: only when the labels do not suffice to tell the user that the fields belong together) is not examined. Elements: in the top document and every readable document nested in it through frames, shadow trees included, every <input> of type radio (compared ignoring ASCII case) that is inside a <form> element or an element with an explicit role="form", and is rendered and exposed in the accessibility tree (no computed display none on it or an ancestor, no computed visibility hidden or collapse, no aria-hidden="true" or inert on it or an ancestor). Radio sets: radios with the same non-empty name attribute and the same form owner, in the same tree (the document or shadow root that holds them). Sets of fewer than two radios, radios without a name, checkboxes, elements with role radio and other fields are not examined. For each set: no fault when one element is an ancestor of every radio of the set, in the flat tree, and is a <fieldset> or has an explicit role of group or radiogroup (the role attribute's first token, compared ignoring ASCII case); otherwise fault on the set. Page result: fault if any set has a fault; otherwise cannot_tell if a nested document cannot be read; otherwise no_fault if at least one set was examined; inapplicable if none was.

For RGAA test 13.2.1. Fault only: it never answers no_fault and never inapplicable. It examines only a target in its initial state (the page as loaded by navigation, no declared step performed); on any other target it answers cannot_tell, since the steps that reached it are user actions. Observation window: from the start of the target's navigation until the engine performs its first action on the page, or until examination ends if it performs none. An action is anything that could count as, or stand in for, a user action: any input event (pointer, mouse, touch, keyboard, wheel), a scroll, a change of viewport size or orientation, moving focus, or a script the engine runs that dispatches events or calls click(), focus() or submit(). Reading the DOM, computed styles, the accessibility tree and taking a screenshot that neither scrolls nor resizes are not actions. The browser must run with its popup blocker disabled, so that a window the page opens without a user gesture is really opened and seen; if the engine cannot confirm this, the page result is cannot_tell. Elements: every new top-level browsing context (a new tab or window, with or without an opener) created in the engine's browser context during the observation window. The engine opens no page itself in that browser context while it examines the target, so any new one comes from the examined page or a document nested in it through frames; if another page of the engine is open in the same browser context, a new context that cannot be attributed to the examined page through its opener gives cannot_tell. For each new browsing context, in this order: (1) If the top document navigated to a new document during the observation window, or if navigator.userActivation.hasBeenActive is true at the end of the window in the top document or in any frame document the engine can read: cannot_tell. This verifies the assumption that no user action happened: sticky activation is never reset within a document, so one reading at the end covers the whole window, and a true value means the opening may follow a user action. (2) If the new context was closed before the end of the observation window: cannot_tell; a window opened and closed at once, for example by a script that probes the browser, is not surely the opening of a new window that the test's wording means. (3) Otherwise: fault on it. A new tab or window that the page opened without any user action and that stayed open is the opening of a new window without the user's action. Windows the engine never sees, because they would open after the observation window or only after an interaction, are not examined, so the check never concludes that no window opens. Dialogs drawn inside the page (modal layers, lightboxes) and alert, confirm or prompt dialogs are not new browsing contexts and are not examined. Page result: fault if any new context reaches (3); otherwise cannot_tell.

For RGAA test 2.1.1. Elements: every <iframe> and <frame> element in the top document and in every document nested in it through frames, shadow trees included. If any nested document cannot be read, answer cannot_tell for the page. For each frame element, in this order: (1) it has a title attribute whose value contains a non-whitespace character: the requirement holds for it. (2) It has a title attribute that is empty or only whitespace: cannot_tell (the wording asks for the attribute; the glossary defines the frame title as its content). (3) It has no title attribute and aria-hidden="true" is set on it, on an ancestor in its document, or on a frame element that hosts that document: cannot_tell, since the exception for technical frames hidden with aria-hidden may apply and deciding it needs judgment. (4) It has no title attribute and is not rendered (computed display none on it or an ancestor, computed visibility hidden or collapse, or inside a frame that is itself not rendered), or is not exposed in the accessibility tree for another reason (inert on it, an ancestor or a hosting frame element included): cannot_tell, since only aria-hidden carries an exception in the official text and no text says whether other hidden frames count. (5) Otherwise: fault on that element. The check ignores aria-label, aria-labelledby and role, which the test does not accept in place of title. Page result: fault if any frame falls under (5); otherwise cannot_tell if any falls under (2), (3) or (4); otherwise no_fault if there is at least one frame; inapplicable if there is no frame element at all.

For RGAA test 2.2.1, the empty-title case only; whether a non-empty title is relevant is not examined. Elements: every <iframe> and <frame> element that has a title attribute, in the top document and in every document nested in it through frames, shadow trees included. Frame elements without a title attribute are outside this test and are not examined. For each element, in this order: (1) An aria-hidden attribute with any value other than false (ignoring ASCII case and surrounding whitespace) is set on it, on an ancestor in its document, or on a frame element that hosts that document: cannot_tell, since the glossary's exception for technical frames hidden with aria-hidden may apply and whether a frame is technical needs judgment. (2) It is not rendered (computed display none on it or an ancestor, computed visibility hidden or collapse, or inside a frame element that is itself not rendered), or it is not exposed in the accessibility tree for another reason (inert on it, an ancestor or a hosting frame element included): cannot_tell, since the text of this test gives no exception for such frames and does not say whether they count. (3) Its title value is empty or made only of ASCII whitespace (U+0009, U+000A, U+000C, U+000D, U+0020): fault on that element. An empty title tells nothing about the frame's content and is not a generic mention, and the frame is not hidden with aria-hidden, so no route and no exception holds. (4) Otherwise cannot_tell: whether a non-empty title is relevant, or a fitting generic mention for a technical frame, is judgment. This includes a value made only of other invisible characters, such as no-break or zero-width spaces. Page result: fault if any element falls under (3); otherwise cannot_tell if any element falls under (1), (2) or (4), or if a nested document cannot be read; otherwise inapplicable, since no frame element has a title attribute. Never no_fault.

For RGAA test 4.3.2. Never faults. Elements: every <track> element whose parent is a <video> or <audio> element, in the top document and in every document nested in it through iframe, frame, object or embed elements, shadow trees included. A <track> element anywhere else delivers nothing to a media and is not examined. Captions a script adds without a <track> element (addTextTrack, a custom player rendering cues from a file it fetches, captions in the media stream) are outside this test, which concerns captions delivered through a <track> element, and are not examined. For each examined track, read its kind IDL attribute, which is the browser's reflection of the kind content attribute (ASCII case-insensitive; a missing attribute reflects as subtitles and an unknown value as metadata). (1) kind is captions: the track is labelled as captions. (2) Any other value: cannot_tell. This includes subtitles (also what a missing attribute gives), descriptions, chapters and metadata, and the singular caption that the methodology spells, which HTML treats as an unknown value. Whether such a track carries captions for deaf and hard-of-hearing users, which would make it fail the test, or translation subtitles or other data, which would leave it outside the test, needs someone to read it, and a custom player may render captions from a metadata track. Page result: cannot_tell if any track falls under (2), or if a nested document or shadow tree cannot be read; otherwise no_fault if at least one track falls under (1): every <track> element the page gives a media is labelled captions, so no media can have captions delivered through a <track> element without kind="captions"; otherwise inapplicable: no <track> element is a child of a media element, so no media has captions delivered through a <track> element. The check does not load the track, count its cues, or establish that its media is a prerecorded synchronized media, so a no_fault page may be one where the test is in fact not applicable (a video-only, live or decorative media, or a track whose file is empty or missing).

For RGAA test 6.1.5, and as evidence only for test 6.1.1. Fault or cannot_tell only: it never answers no_fault and never inapplicable. Elements: in the top document only, shadow trees included, every HTML element with an href attribute that has no role attribute, no aria-labelledby attribute, and an aria-label attribute whose value N holds a character other than whitespace. Links in frames, SVG links, elements with role="link" and links without such an aria-label are not examined. For each element, in this order: (1) cannot_tell when the element is not rendered or is not exposed in the accessibility tree as a link (aria-hidden="true" or inert on it or an ancestor included). (2) cannot_tell when the element or a descendant is an , , ,

For RGAA test 6.2.1. Elements: in the top document and every document nested in it through frames, shadow trees included, every HTML element with an href attribute, every SVG element with an href or xlink:href attribute, and every element with an explicit role="link". An without href or xlink:href is an anchor and is skipped (technical note of criterion 6.2). If a nested document cannot be read, answer cannot_tell for the page. For each element, compute its name from content only, ignoring aria-labelledby, aria-label, title and xlink:title on the element itself: walk its descendants, skip every subtree that is hidden from assistive technologies (aria-hidden="true", computed display none, computed visibility hidden or collapse, the hidden attribute), and collect: the data of text nodes; for an or an element with role img or image, its text alternative from aria-labelledby, then aria-label, then alt, then title; for an inline

For RGAA test 7.3.2. Evidence only. Runs in the keyboard pass. Elements: every element that receives focus while the Tab key moves through the page's sequential focus order, in the top document, shadow trees included, and in nested frame documents that can be read. For each one: record the deep active element (through shadow roots and readable frames) right after the key press; then wait 500 ms with no input and read it again. Fault on the element when focus is now on the document body or on no element, while the element is still connected, rendered, not disabled, not inert and still focusable: its focus was removed without user action. cannot_tell for the element when focus has moved to another element or into a frame, or when the element was removed, hidden, disabled or made inert meanwhile (whether these count as removing focus is not decided here). Elements that can take focus only from a pointer are not examined, and the particular case of criterion 7.3 is not examined. Page result: fault if any element has a fault; otherwise cannot_tell if any element is cannot_tell or the pass did not complete; otherwise no_fault; inapplicable when no element receives focus.

For RGAA test 7.3.1. Evidence only. Elements: in the top document, shadow trees included, every element with an event listener attached directly to it for click, dblclick, mousedown, mouseup, pointerdown, pointerup, touchstart, touchend, keydown, keyup or keypress, read through the DevTools protocol (DOMDebugger.getEventListeners, which includes on* attributes). Fault on such an element when it is rendered, not disabled, not inert, not in the sequential focus order (not natively focusable and without tabindex, or with a negative tabindex), and has no ancestor that is in the sequential focus order. cannot_tell for such an element when an ancestor is in the sequential focus order (keyboard activation of the ancestor may perform the same action). Listeners attached to window, document, html or body cannot be attributed to elements: when any of the event types above is listened for there, the page result is cannot_tell unless a fault exists. A fault says only that Tab cannot reach the element; it says nothing about an equivalent element elsewhere in the page, keyboard shortcuts, pointer access, or the particular case of criterion 7.3. Page result: fault if any element has a fault; otherwise cannot_tell as above; otherwise no_fault; inapplicable when no element has such a listener.

For RGAA test 8.10.1. Faults a page only on visible right-to-left text that no element with a dir attribute contains; it never answers no_fault. Scope: the tree of the top-level document only, not shadow trees, template contents or documents in frames. Document conditions, all required, otherwise cannot_tell: (D1) document.contentType is text/html, the document element is an HTML html element and the body is an HTML body element; (D2) the html element carries a lang attribute or an attribute named xml:lang, and each of the two that is present has a value that, ignoring ASCII case, is a language subtag optionally followed by a hyphen and a region subtag of two letters or three digits, with nothing else (no script subtag), where the language subtag is on the pinned list of languages written only from left to right: fr, en, de, es, it, pt, nl, ca, eu, br, co, oc, gl, da, sv, nb, nn, no, fi, is, et, lv, lt, pl, cs, sk, sl, hr, hu, ro, bg, ru, uk, el, mt, ga, cy, gd, lb, sq, mk, tr, zh, ja, ko, vi, th (record the list's version with the check); (D3) neither html nor body carries a dir attribute in any form; (D4) html and body have computed direction ltr. Witness: a text node that meets conditions (c) exposure, (d) font, (e) paint, (f) contrast and (g) geometry of the witness definition of custom/8-3-default-lang-present, read as written there, and the two conditions below, which replace (a) and (b). (A) Place: it is in the top-level document's tree, inside body; every element strictly between body and the node is an HTML element from this list: div, main, article, section, header, footer, nav, aside, address, p, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, ul, ol, li, dl, dt, dd, blockquote, figure, figcaption, table, caption, thead, tbody, tfoot, tr, td, th, span, em, strong, b, i, u, s, small, mark, abbr, cite, q, dfn, time, sub, sup, ins, del, a, button, label (bdi, bdo and every element not listed are excluded); neither body nor any of those elements is a shadow host or carries a role, aria-hidden, hidden or inert attribute, in any form or with any value; and each of them has computed direction ltr and computed unicode-bidi normal. (B) Letters: its data holds two characters of Unicode general category L in a row whose Bidi_Class is R or AL, with only characters of category M between them. Uncovered witness: a witness none of whose ancestor elements, body and html included, carries a dir attribute in any form, even empty. Answer: fault when D1 to D4 hold and the page holds an uncovered witness, reported on the first in tree order. That node is visible, exposed text in a script that reads from right to left. The document's language, from the list, reads from left to right, and with no dir on html, body or any parent the default reading direction is left to right, so it differs from the default under both the methodology's comparison (with the document's language) and the glossary's (with the dir attribute, ltr when absent); and no element containing it has a dir attribute. Otherwise cannot_tell: the check does not look at attribute values, field values, text generated by CSS, framed documents, shadow trees or text that fails a witness condition, so it never shows that every right-to-left text is covered, nor that there is none. Never inapplicable.

For RGAA test 8.10.2, the condition that the dir value is conforming (rtl or ltr) only; relevance is not examined. It never answers no_fault. Scope, document conditions D1 to D4 and witness conditions as defined for custom/8-10-rtl-text-dir-missing, with one change: in condition (A), the requirement that each element between body and the node has computed direction ltr and unicode-bidi normal is dropped (a dir attribute below body changes them by design); body must still meet it through D4 and its own computed unicode-bidi normal. Governing element of a witness: its nearest ancestor element that carries a dir attribute in any form. By D3 it is neither html nor body. Answer: fault when D1 to D4 hold and some witness has a governing element whose dir value, with leading and trailing ASCII whitespace removed and ASCII letters lowercased, is not empty and is neither rtl nor ltr (for example auto, right or rlt); reported on the first such witness in tree order, with the element and its value. That witness is a right-to-left passage contained in an element whose dir attribute gives its reading direction, so it is a passage validated at 8.10.1 and that dir attribute is a change of reading direction, and its value is not one of the two the wording and the glossary allow. Otherwise cannot_tell. In particular, a value that is empty or whitespace only is never a fault (the wording does not say whether such an attribute is a change of reading direction), nor is a value that equals rtl or ltr only after removing whitespace or lowercasing (the wording gives the values in lower case and does not say whether case or spacing matters), nor a dir attribute on an element that contains no witness. Never inapplicable.

For RGAA test 8.2.1, the condition that id values are unique in the page only; the other four conditions are not examined. It never answers no_fault. Scope: the tree of the top-level document only, read on the target as established and before any other check changes the DOM. Not examined: shadow trees, the contents of template elements, documents in frames, text inside noscript. (1) If document.doctype is null, answer cannot_tell: the test applies "pour chaque déclaration de type de document", and the DOM cannot show whether the source holds a declaration the parser dropped. (2) Otherwise collect every element of the document tree in the HTML, SVG or MathML namespace that has an attribute in no namespace whose local name is id and whose value holds at least one character other than ASCII whitespace. Visibility, rendering and exposure to assistive technologies do not matter: the test is about the generated source code, which holds every element of the document tree, hidden or not. (3) Fault when two collected elements have values that are equal code point for code point; report the first such pair in tree order, with the value. Values that differ only in case, empty values and whitespace-only values are never a fault. (4) Otherwise cannot_tell: the check does not examine template contents, shadow trees or framed documents, so it never shows that every id in the page is unique. Never inapplicable.

For RGAA test 8.3.1. Scope: the top-level document of the page; documents in frames are read only for step 1. Document type: XHTML 1.1 when the doctype public identifier contains "XHTML 1.1"; XHTML 1.0 when it contains "XHTML 1.0", split by the served content type (document.contentType) into text/html and application/xhtml+xml; other XML when it contains "XHTML" otherwise or the document is served as application/xhtml+xml without one of those doctypes; otherwise HTML. Indication required on an element: HTML: lang; XHTML 1.0 as text/html: lang and xml:lang; XHTML 1.0 as application/xhtml+xml: xml:lang; XHTML 1.1: xml:lang; other XML: lang and xml:lang. xml:lang is read with getAttributeNS("http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace", "lang") in XML documents and as the attribute named xml:lang in text/html documents. An element carries the indication when every required attribute is present with a value holding a non-whitespace character. The check answers no_fault only through the html element. It never concludes that every text element carries the indication: the wording "chaque élément de texte" does not say which texts count (a field's value, text generated by CSS, alternative and title attributes, the page title, the text of framed documents), so no list of text items can be shown complete. Witness: a text node that is a text element under any reading of the wording, so that a fault never rests on text that could be decorative, hidden, invisible or a pictogram. A text node is a witness only when all of the following hold; a node that fails any of them is never a witness, whatever it holds. (a) Place: it is in the top-level document's tree, not in a shadow tree, inside body; body is an HTML element, and every element strictly between body and the node is an HTML element from this list: div, main, article, section, header, footer, nav, aside, address, center, p, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, ul, ol, li, dl, dt, dd, blockquote, figure, figcaption, table, caption, thead, tbody, tfoot, tr, td, th, span, em, strong, b, i, u, s, small, big, mark, abbr, cite, q, dfn, time, data, sub, sup, ins, del, bdi, font; and neither body nor any of those elements is a shadow host or carries a role, aria-hidden, hidden or inert attribute, in any form or with any value. (b) Letters: its data holds two characters of Unicode general category L in a row, with only characters of category M between them. (c) Exposure: Chromium's full accessibility tree holds a node for it (static text whose backend DOM node is this text node) that is not ignored. (d) Font: every family in the computed font-family of its parent element is either one of the unquoted generic families serif, sans-serif, monospace, system-ui, ui-serif, ui-sans-serif and ui-monospace, or, quotes removed and ignoring ASCII case, a family on the pinned list of text fonts: Arial, Helvetica, Helvetica Neue, Times, Times New Roman, Georgia, Verdana, Tahoma, Trebuchet MS, Courier, Courier New, Lucida Grande, Lucida Sans Unicode, Segoe UI, Calibri, Cambria, Garamond, Palatino, Palatino Linotype, Book Antiqua, Geneva, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Roboto, Noto Sans, Noto Serif, DejaVu Sans, DejaVu Serif, Liberation Sans, Liberation Serif, Ubuntu, Cantarell (record the list's version with the check; it holds only fonts whose letter glyphs are letters, never an icon or symbol font); and document.fonts holds no FontFace whose family matches, ignoring ASCII case, any family in that computed font-family. This rules out icon fonts, whether they draw a pictogram from a word by ligature or from a single letter, symbol fonts such as Wingdings or Webdings, and any family the page defines itself. (e) Paint: the parent element and every ancestor element have computed opacity 1, filter none, mix-blend-mode normal, clip-path none, mask-image none and clip auto; the parent element has computed visibility visible, -webkit-text-security none, a font-size of at least 8 CSS pixels, and a color and -webkit-text-fill-color with alpha 1. (f) Contrast: walk from the parent element up its ancestors to the first whose computed background-color has alpha 1; no element on that walk, that one included, has a background-image other than none or a background-color with alpha strictly between 0 and 1. If no element up to html has an opaque background-color, the background is white, but only when the html element's computed color-scheme is normal; otherwise the node is not a witness. If the parent's computed -webkit-text-fill-color differs from its computed color, the node is not a witness, since the painted fill is what counts and the color alone would misstate the contrast; otherwise the contrast ratio (WCAG 2 formula) between the parent's color, which is then the painted fill, and that background is at least 2. (g) Geometry: take the rectangles Range.getClientRects() returns for the node; clip each to the padding box of every ancestor element whose computed overflow-x or overflow-y is not visible or whose computed contain includes paint, content or strict (whether or not that ancestor is its containing block), and to the viewport as loaded, without scrolling. At least one clipped rectangle is at least 4 CSS pixels wide and 4 high, and at its centre document.elementFromPoint returns the node's parent element itself (not a child, an ancestor or any other element painted above the text). No element other than the parent and its ancestors whose computed pointer-events is none has a border box containing that centre, since hit testing skips such an element although it may paint over the text. The parent element generates no ::before or ::after box (computed content none or normal for both), since hit testing reports a pseudo-element as its element. Uncovered witness: a witness with no lang or xml:lang attribute in any form, even empty, on any ancestor element. Answer, in this order: (1) The html element of the top-level document carries the indication its document type requires: no_fault, unless the page holds a rendered iframe or frame (with a layout box, in the top-level document or in a document nested through frames, shadow trees included) whose document cannot be read, or whose document holds a rendered or exposed text node with a non-whitespace character while its html element does not carry the indication its own document type requires; then cannot_tell (the wording does not say whether a framed document counts as part of the page for this test). (2) The html element has a lang or xml:lang attribute in any form (empty, whitespace only, or not the one its document type requires): cannot_tell. (3) The html element has neither a lang nor an xml:lang attribute in any form, and the page holds at least one uncovered witness: fault, reported on the first in tree order. That node is visible and exposed text in ordinary content, with no language indication on any parent, so the second route fails for it whichever texts are counted, and the first route fails because html has neither attribute. (4) Otherwise cannot_tell: the html element has neither attribute and no witness is uncovered. Either the second route may hold, but the check cannot show that every text element is covered; or the only text without a language source is not a witness: hidden from assistive technologies or not exposed, invisible though laid out (opacity below 1, transparent or low-contrast colour, clipped, off-screen, covered, too small), drawn in an icon, symbol or page-defined font, a single letter, inside a link, control, label, code, ruby, SVG, MathML, shadow tree or an element with a role, outside body, in an attribute, a field's value, generated by CSS, or in a framed document. Never inapplicable.

For RGAA test 8.4.1, the validity condition only (relevance is not examined). Scope: the html element of the top-level document, with the document types, required attributes and way of reading xml:lang defined for custom/8-3-default-lang-present. For each required attribute present on the html element: if its value is empty or has leading or trailing whitespace, cannot_tell for it. Otherwise take the part of the value before the first hyphen (the whole value if there is none) and compare it, ignoring ASCII case, with a pinned list holding every ISO 639-1 code, every ISO 639-2 code in both its bibliographic and terminologic forms (including the reserved range qaa to qtz and the codes mis, mul, und and zxx), every ISO 639-3 code and every ISO 639-5 code, plus codes since deprecated or withdrawn from any of those parts (such as iw, in, ji, mo); record the list's version with the check. Fault on the attribute when that part is not in the list. When the html element has none of the required attributes, answer cannot_tell: the default language may be given on each text element instead, which this check does not examine, or be missing, in which case this test does not apply. Attributes on html that the document type does not require are not examined. Page result: fault if any required attribute has a fault; no_fault when every required attribute is present and its code is in the list; otherwise cannot_tell. Never inapplicable.

For RGAA test 8.5.1. Scope: the top-level document, read on the target as established; documents in frames are read only in step 3. Title element: an element in the HTML namespace whose local name is title (an SVG or MathML title is not one). Qualifying text: the concatenated text of the element's descendant text nodes holds at least one character of Unicode general category L or N that is not on the pinned list of blank-looking characters U+115F, U+1160, U+3164 and U+FFA0 (record the list's version with the check). Answer in this order. (1) If document.contentType is neither text/html nor application/xhtml+xml, or the document element is not an HTML html element, cannot_tell: for example an image, a text file or a PDF that the browser wraps in a page of its own. (2) If the document tree holds no title element, no template element's content holds one, no shadow tree of the document holds one, and no noscript element's text contains the string <title in any ASCII case: fault. The page as examined has no title element anywhere, so it has no page title under any reading. (3) If the first title element of the document tree in tree order (the one document.title reads) is a child of the head element document.head returns, and its text qualifies: no_fault, unless the page holds a rendered iframe or frame (one with a layout box, in the top-level document or in a document nested through frames, shadow trees included) whose document cannot be read, or whose document holds a text node with a non-whitespace character that is rendered (has a client rectangle) or exposed in the accessibility tree while that document has no title element, child of its head, whose text qualifies; then cannot_tell, because the wording does not say whether a framed document is a web page for this test. (4) Otherwise cannot_tell: the first title element is empty, holds only whitespace, punctuation, symbols or blank-looking characters, or is not a child of head; or the only title elements are in template contents, shadow trees or noscript text. The wording does not say whether such an element gives the page a title. Never inapplicable.

For RGAA test 9.1.2. Scope: the top-level document, read on the target as established, shadow trees included; documents in frames are not examined. Candidates: every h1, h2, h3, h4, h5 and h6 element in the HTML namespace, and every element whose role attribute has heading (ASCII case-insensitive) as its first token the browser recognises. A witness is a candidate that meets every condition below. (a) It is an h1 to h6 element, or it has an aria-level attribute whose value is a string of ASCII digits with a value of at least 1. (b) It is present and not ignored in the browser's accessibility tree, with the role heading; so it is rendered, and neither it nor an ancestor carries aria-hidden="true" or inert. (c) It has no descendant element other than br and wbr, and none of its descendant text nodes holds a character other than ASCII whitespace. (d) It has no aria-label, aria-labelledby, aria-owns or title attribute. (e) The computed content of the element itself and of its ::before and ::after pseudo-elements is none or normal. (f) Its computed background-image is none. (g) Its computed accessible name is empty. Page result: fault if any witness exists, naming each one; otherwise cannot_tell. The check never answers no_fault or inapplicable. A candidate that fails any of (a) to (g) is left undecided on purpose: a heading role without a valid aria-level (the wording does not say whether it is a heading); a heading that is not rendered or not exposed (the test gives no exception for hidden headings and does not say whether they count); a heading holding an element, a label attribute, generated content or a background image (its content may be given that way); text made only of invisible or no-break characters.

For RGAA test 9.1.3, as evidence only. Scope: the top-level document, read on the target as established, shadow trees included. Elements: every element that is not an h1 to h6 element in the HTML namespace and whose role attribute has heading (ASCII case-insensitive) as its first token the browser recognises. Fault on each such element that has no aria-level attribute, or one whose value is not a string of ASCII digits with a value of at least 1; for each, record whether it is rendered and whether it is exposed in the accessibility tree. Page result: fault if any element is faulted, naming each one; no_fault otherwise. Never inapplicable. A fault says only that an element declared as a heading uses neither markup the methodology of 9.1.3 accepts. Whether it is a passage of text constituting a heading is left to a human.

For RGAA test 9.2.1, the requirement that the main content zone is structured with a <main> element. Scope: the top-level document, read on the target as established. Answer in this order. (1) If document.contentType is neither text/html nor application/xhtml+xml, or the document element is not an HTML html element: cannot_tell. (2) If document.doctype is null: cannot_tell; the particular case does not say whether a page that declares no doctype falls under it. (3) If the doctype is not the HTML5 doctype, that is its name is not html in any ASCII case, or its publicId is not empty, or its systemId is neither empty nor about:legacy-compat: inapplicable (particular case of criterion 9.2). (4) If a main element in the HTML namespace exists anywhere in the document tree or in a shadow tree, rendered or not: cannot_tell. (5) If an element in the document tree or a shadow tree has a role attribute holding the token main in any ASCII case: cannot_tell. (6) If the document has a frameset element, or holds a rendered iframe, frame, object or embed element (one with a layout box), shadow trees included: cannot_tell, since the main content may be in a nested document and the wording does not say whether that document is part of the page here. (7) A witness text is a text node of the body, shadow trees included, that holds a Unicode letter, has a client rectangle of non-zero width and height, belongs to an element that is present and not ignored in the accessibility tree, and has no ancestor (crossing shadow boundaries) that is a header, footer, nav, aside or dialog element or has a role attribute holding the token banner, contentinfo, navigation, complementary, search, dialog or alertdialog. If there is no witness text: cannot_tell. (8) Otherwise: fault, naming one witness text. The page then shows content outside its header, navigation, footer and secondary zones, so it has a main content zone, and no <main> element structures it. The check never answers no_fault.

For RGAA test 9.2.1, the requirement that the document uses a single visible <main> element. Scope: the top-level document tree, read on the target as established; main elements in shadow trees, in template contents or in framed documents are not counted. Answer in this order. (1) If document.contentType is neither text/html nor application/xhtml+xml, or the document element is not an HTML html element: cannot_tell. (2) If document.doctype is null: cannot_tell; the particular case does not say whether a page that declares no doctype falls under it. (3) If the doctype is not the HTML5 doctype, that is its name is not html in any ASCII case, or its publicId is not empty, or its systemId is neither empty nor about:legacy-compat: inapplicable (particular case of criterion 9.2). (4) A main element in the HTML namespace is shown when all of these hold: neither it nor any ancestor has a hidden attribute; it is present and not ignored in the accessibility tree with the role main, so it is rendered and neither it nor an ancestor carries aria-hidden="true" or inert; its computed visibility is visible and its computed content-visibility is not hidden; the computed opacity of it and of every ancestor is 1; neither it nor any ancestor has a computed clip-path other than none or a clip other than auto; and it contains a text node holding a Unicode letter or digit whose client rectangle has non-zero width and height and lies at least in part inside the document's scrollable area (from the origin to scrollWidth and scrollHeight) and inside the padding box of every ancestor whose overflow clips. (5) If two or more main elements are shown: fault, naming them. Two <main> elements are then visible and exposed to assistive technologies at once, neither with a hidden attribute, which breaks the single visible <main> under every reading of the wording, the methodology and the technical note. (6) Otherwise: cannot_tell. The check never answers no_fault.
